results.name: rule_based
results.note: rule_based.py matches Swahili keyword phrases (keywords.py / SYMPTOM_MAP) against symptom_text. saca_test.csv's symptom_text is English, so extract_symptoms() returns [] on almost every row, and rule_based.py's own fallback ("no symptoms recognised" → LOW) fires nearly universally. The 8.64% accuracy equals the LOW-tier share of the test set (85/984) — this is not a measurement of the classifier's real-world quality, it is a language mismatch between a Swahili production classifier and an English test set. Verified by re-running score_classifiers.py directly against the corrected saca_test.csv/saca_train.csv in this session (2026-09-09). Do not use this number to judge rule_based.py; it needs a Swahili-labelled test set to be evaluated meaningfully (see handoff doc: unverified 29-term Swahili glossary draft).
